published_statement: 2022 paper, Table XXXII: c = 299 792 458 m s^-1 exact; G = 6.674 30(15)e-11 m^3 kg^-1 s^-2, u_r = 2.2e-5; h = 6.626 070 15e-34 exact, hbar = 1.054 571 817 ...e-34 exact; e = 1.602 176 634e-19 exact; k = 1.380 649e-23 exact; mu_0 = 1.256 637 061 27(20)e-6; eps_0 = 8.854 187 8188(14)e-12; m_e = 9.109 383 7139(28)e-31; m_p = 1.672 621 925 95(52)e-27; m_p/m_e = 1836.152 673 426(32) u_r 1.7e-11; alpha^-1 = 137.035 999 177(21); a_0 = 5.291 772 105 44(82)e-11; E_h = 4.359 744 722 2060(48)e-18; l_P = 1.616 255(18)e-35 u_r 1.1e-5; u = 1.660 539 068 92(52)e-27. Sec. I.B.11: 'the 16 values of G ... Since there is no new value, the same 3.9 expansion factor applied ... in 2018 ... is also used in 2022; the 2022 and 2018 recommended values of G are therefore identical.' Sec. XVI.A: alpha decreased 'by 4.5 times its 2018 uncertainty', moving 15 of 43 listed constants. Prsa 2016 Table 1: (GM)_sun^N = 1.327 124 4e20 m^3 s^-2, 'by definition exact ... conversion factors only'; rec. 5: 'if SI masses are explicitly needed, they should be expressed in terms of (GM)_object/G, where the estimate of G should be specified'. Libralato 2025 Table 2: Gaia DR3 parallax of Proxima 768.067 +- 0.050 mas.
published_hypotheses: c, h (hence hbar), e, k, N_A are exact by the 2019 SI definition; their 'values' carry no uncertainty (2022 Table XXXII, Pavese p.5)

G is the weighted mean of 16 mutually inconsistent laboratory determinations (Table XXX, 1982-2019) with uncertainties expanded by 3.9 so that every normalised residual is <= 2; u_r = 2.2e-5 is that expanded figure (Sec. XV.A: chi^2 = 12.9 for 15 d.o.f. after expansion; BIPM-14 and JILA-18 residuals 7.75 and -6.80 before it)

alpha and everything tied to it (mu_0, eps_0, m_e, a_0, u, m_p) come from the least-squares adjustment of 133 input data with expansion factors 1.7 and 2.5 on subsets; the 2018 alpha rested on the 2011 LKB h/m(Rb) datum later found to carry uncorrectable systematics (Sec. XVI.C.1)
IAU 2015 B3 nominalises (GM)_sun, R_sun, L_sun, T_sun -- NOT M_sun in kg; a kg solar mass is (GM)^N/G and inherits G's uncertainty and G's CODATA year
the light year is not an IAU-defined unit in Prsa 2016; it is c x one Julian year (365.25 d) by convention -- exact given c and the Julian year

Gaia DR3 astrometry is the EDR3 solution (34 months), with a magnitude/colour/latitude-dependent parallax zero point of order -17 to -40 uas that is NOT applied in the catalogue value, and poorly mapped for G <~ 9 (Proxima G ~ 8.98)

lacked_data: Tested for this result. What the CODATA 2018 task group had: 16 G determinations to 2019 (Table XXX), the 2011 LKB and 2018 Berkeley atom-recoil data for alpha, and the 2019-SI exact h, e, k, N_A. What came later: (a) for G, NOTHING -- no new determination entered the 2022 adjustment, and the 2026 literature still cites 2.2e-5; the latent problem is not missing data but mutually inconsistent data (Q = 198/15 d.o.f.; BIPM-14 at +7.75 sigma before expansion), so the 'true' G could differ from 6.67430e-11 by a few 1e-5 and by 1.9e-4 if BIPM is right; (b) for alpha, YES -- the 2020 LKB Rb-recoil measurement exposed 'significant systematic effects in the earlier LKB experiment that could not be corrected retroactively' and moved the recommended alpha by 4.5 of its stated 2018 sigmas, dragging mu_0, eps_0, m_e, a_0, u, m_p with it. So M's hypothesis is CONFIRMED in kind for this result: a published recommended value did move by more than its stated uncertainty when a datum the authors lacked arrived. Whether it changes any conclusion: NO, computed -- the moves are 7e-10..1.4e-9 relative (script 5), the largest possible G move ~2e-4, and the board's claims resting on these constants are pinned at 1e-4..1e-3 and argued at margins of 10 to 42 orders (branelink's SME null, achievable's 71.256 orders, throatmass's 32.31 orders). For the Proxima distance, later data (HST 2025) agree at 1.2 sigma; the un-applied Gaia zero point (2-5e-5) is the only named systematic and it too touches the fifth figure only. Evidence against a larger effect: the 2022 adjustment's Table XXXVIII lists no constant the tree uses that moved by more than 5 sigma or by more than 1.4e-9 relative.
grade_evidence: Every constant the 32 owner sites type is the value its cited source gives (c, hbar, e, k_B exact per 2019 SI; G, alpha, mu_0, eps_0, m_e, m_p, u, a_0, E_h, l_P per CODATA 2018 as restated by Fayet 1906.05123 and fixed by the 2022 paper's Table XXXVIII, script 5b; (GM)^N per IAU 2015 B3; LY, au, pc, Julian year exact; Proxima 768.067 mas per Gaia DR3 as restated by 2512.08533). Every derived figure the ledger and selftests pin is reproduced from those constants (script sections 1-5, all MUST checks pass). No moved datum moves a conclusion: G is unchanged 2018->2022 and its full sigma moves G-bearing figures by 2.2e-5; the CODATA 2022 shifts move alpha-family figures by <= 1.4e-9; both are below every owner tolerance and 10+ orders below every margin. The discrepancies found are misprint-class and recorded, not refutations: three solar-mass literals (1.98840 / 1.98847 / 1.98892e30, spread 2.6e-4) with the 'IAU nominal' label naming a G-dependent derivation; four light-year roundings; a truncated m_p; no uncertainty carried anywhere; a drivensource pin at 1e-9 that holds at 5.4e-10. The tree's own status words are honest where they exist ('NAMED-NOT-READ' at address, massform, warpfolder) and absent where a bare literal is used.
what_would_change_the_grade: NARROWED if any owner is found to pin a physical claim (not a reproducibility fixture) at better than 2.2e-5 in a G-bearing quantity or 1.4e-9 in an alpha-bearing one -- none was found among the 32 sites. DATA-DEPENDENT if a future CODATA adjustment moved G by more than ~1e-3 (i.e. beyond phase1's coarsest tolerance), which the 16-datum spread (max outlier +1.9e-4) makes implausible, or if Gaia DR4 (Dec 2026) moved Proxima's parallax by more than 5e-4 (HST 2025 already bounds it at 4e-4). WRONG only if a typed literal were shown not to be its source's value -- checked and excluded for every site except phase1's 1.98892e30, which is a stale textbook value, a discrepancy and not a refutation of anything resting on it. The label 'IAU nominal' on M_SUN and phase1's solar mass are the two items a repair pass could name; this audit repairs nothing.
